Visitors but no sales, no add to carts?

You have visitors but no sales: people land on the store and nobody adds anything to the cart. Here is what we see when we look at stores with this problem, and what to check today.

What store owners post

I ran a paid meta ad campaign over the weekend and gained 260 sessions but 0 add to carts.
Traffic but 0 sales.

Quoted from public merchant forums, names removed.

What we see when we look at stores

  • At 45% of the 99 stores we could measure, the product pages do not clearly state both shipping and returns. A buyer who cannot see the delivery cost or the return terms has a reason to leave.
  • The median store's median product description is 69 words, and at 80% of stores fewer than 85% of products reach 80 words. A short description leaves the "is this right for me?" question unanswered.
  • At 57% of stores, fewer than half the product photos have a description for people who cannot see them, and at 21 stores the review stars only appear after the page finishes loading, which Google may not see.
  • We also opened 15 stores whose owners had asked a public feedback board why they were not getting sales. 9 of 15 showed no reviews on the sampled product page, 9 of 15 had at least one of their first five descriptions under 80 words, and 4 of 15 had a shipping or refund policy that was missing, thin or still template text. Those owners picked themselves and 15 is a small number, so read it as direction.
  • These are gaps we measured, not proof that they cause lost sales. Neither check looked at visitors or how many of them buy.

Numbers are from our 100-store study (3 October 2026, public pages only, a hand-picked sample).

What other store owners were told when they asked for feedback: the store feedback study.

Three questions, answered one by one

  • Why do I get traffic but no add to carts on my Shopify store?
  • I have a Shopify store and no sales yet. What should I check first?
  • Could my shipping and return policy pages be why people do not buy?

Check it today, no purchase

  1. Open your best-selling product page on your phone, as a stranger would. Can you find the delivery cost, the delivery time and the return terms without leaving the page?
  2. Read the first screen of the description. Does it say what the product is, what it is made of or how it fits, and who it is for?
  3. Check that the page matches the ad or post that brought people: same product, same price, same offer.
  4. Look for reviews or any other proof from real buyers on the product page itself.
  5. Open your refund, shipping and privacy policies. Do they agree with each other and with the FAQ? Contradictions read as a warning sign.
  6. Send one friend who has never seen the store to a product page and ask what they would worry about before paying.

Questions store owners ask

Why do I get traffic but 0 add to carts?

Usually the visitors cannot answer a basic question on the product page: what exactly is it, what does it cost in total with delivery, what happens if it is wrong. Open the page on your phone and try to answer those three questions in 30 seconds. If you cannot, neither can they. Also check that the ad's promise matches the page.

Is 260 sessions with no add to carts enough to judge my store?

It is enough to know something is off, not enough to know what. Look at where the sessions came from: ad traffic that clicks by accident behaves differently from search or email. Compare the landing page to the ad, and fix the obvious page problems before spending more.

Should I just offer a discount?

Not first. One merchant in a forum reported 10% off converting at about 4% and 20% off falling to about 2.5%. That is one store, not a rule, but it shows a bigger discount does not automatically convert better. Trust and clear delivery and return terms come first.

Could my traffic be fake or bots?

It can be. Signs are sessions from countries you do not advertise to, or thousands of add to carts an hour on a small store. Check the country and source split in your analytics. If real buyers get no add to carts, bots are not your problem.

How do I get honest feedback on my store?

Ask three people who have never seen it to open one product page and say what would stop them buying. You can also send us your store address and we will send back one page of findings, free, from the public pages.
